messages:
maya: Heads-up — marketing reserved a week-long promotional ramp in early June. Forecast shows a ~3.2x peak vs baseline for low-latency text-gen routes. Need quick sanity-check: how much GPU headroom + safety cushion to keep p95/p99 under SLOs. Can someone run a back-of-envelope and call out blockers?

sam: I pulled the basic numbers. Baseline: 350 active GPUs avg, typical batch efficiency ~2.1, avg tokens per request 45, req/s baseline ~350 rps. Peak rps estimate ~1120 rps (3.2x).

li: For p95 target we're fine with batching scaling, p99 is where queueing shows. Network tail in eu-west has been adding ~80–120ms spikes which eats our latency budget. If that repeats during ramp we'll need buffer GPUs.

julio: Quick calc I did in Slack:
```
# rough capacity calc
req_per_sec = 1120
tokens_per_req = 45
tokens_per_gpu_sec = 2200   # measured effective token throughput per GPU at current kernel/quant setup
batching_eff = 2.1
effective_tps = req_per_sec * tokens_per_req
gpus_required = ceil(effective_tps / (tokens_per_gpu_sec * batching_eff))
# plug numbers -> gpus_required ≈ ceil(1120*45 / (2200*2.1)) ≈ ceil(50400 / 4620) ≈ 11 (this is per subcluster slice)
```
Note: that 11 is per logical serving shard for that workload; aggregate across all shards we currently run ~320 for production models (so this calc maps to a subset).

sam: That fragment is helpful. When we project cluster-wide: if baseline 350 -> naive scaling gives ~1120/350 ≈ 3.2x -> ~1120 GPUs. But because of batching_eff multiplier you get less linear scale. Using Julio's approach across all traffic: gpus_total ≈ ceil(baseline_effective_tokens * 3.2 / (tokens_per_gpu_sec * batching_eff)). I estimate ~870–940 GPUs required to maintain current latency medians, but p99 needs ~1.15x more due to queueing tail (so ~1000–1080 GPUs).

li: +1 to adding tail multiplier. Also add a regional network safety factor: eu-west historical interconnect drops increased retry churn by ~7% during prior campaigns. Account for an extra 7% headroom for that region or route traffic away.

maya: Cost perspective — finance said reserved GPU-hour pricing is $1.95/hr for our committed assets, on-demand equivalent ~ $3.10/hr. If we plan for 1k GPUs sustained for 7 days: cost_delta_on_demand = (3.10-1.95)*1000*24*7 ≈ $1.0M for that burst week. Need to weigh against promo revenue.

oncall-bot: Incident note: last week eu-west interconnect had 12m of elevated RTT at 2026-02-14T03:22Z that correlated with p99 spikes. (link: https://infra.internal/incidents/9876)

julio: Proposals: 1) Add 18% buffer over Julio's capacity calc for p99+network tail during the promo window (fits the 1.15 * 1.07 composite). 2) Pre-warm an extra 150 GPUs in eu-west as a hot spare pool to avoid coldstart queuing. 3) Enable lightweight fallback (smaller model) for best-effort, non-critical routes at 95th percentile.

sam: Operational checklist:
- schedule prewarm start 24h before peak
- bump autoscaler max limit to 1200 GPUs for the campaign window
- add A/B route rule to offload non-SLA traffic to cheaper quantized model
- validate KV cache priming script (li, can you own?)

li: I’ll own cache priming and a quick simulated arrival test tomorrow. I’ll also run a short queuing sim (M/M/c approx) to sanity-check tail multiplier and post results here.

maya: Great. If sim shows >18% tail risk we take Julio's route. Who can draft the exec note for finance with the estimated cost delta and risk options? (cc @julio) :eyes:

julio: I’ll draft it — will include two scenarios: conservative (940 GPUs + 18% buffer) and aggressive (1080 GPUs) with cost numbers and rollback plan.

sam: One more ask: include a simple admission-control knob we can flip during the window. Policy: if queue depth > X for > 10s then reject/route non-critical requests. We should document X with the sim results.

maya: Thanks team — we’ll reconvene after li's sim and Julio’s finance note.
